instruction: Rigid Body Dominoes `scene.blend` contains: - A static ground plate `Ground` (20x2 BU, top at z = 0) with a PASSIVE rigid body. - 10 upright domino plates `Domino01..Domino10`, each with dimensions 0.2 (X) x 1.0 (Y) x 2.0 (Z), centered at `(x_i, 0, 1.0)` where `x_i = -4.5 + i * 1.0` for `i` in `0..9`. That is, bottoms resting on z = 0, spaced 1.0 BU apart along +X. - Each domino has an ACTIVE rigid body with `mass=1.0`, `friction=0.8`, `restitution=0.1`. - Scene `frame_start = 1`, `frame_end = 150`. A rigid body world exists but the simulation has NOT been baked. make the chain topple. Concretely: 1. Give `Domino01` a small initial tilt about the Y axis (e.g., rotate it by ~0.2 rad / ~11 deg about +Y, or something in the same ballpark that is enough to make it unambiguously fall in the +X direction rather than balance). The Blender rigid-body API does not expose an initial linear velocity, so the simplest way to start the chain reaction is to tilt `Domino01` slightly before simulation. 2. Bake the rigid body simulation with `bpy.ops.ptcache.bake_all(bake=True)`. 3. Bake the simulation results to keyframes on all 10 dominoes: select them all, call `bpy.ops.rigidbody.bake_to_keyframes(frame_start=1, frame_end=120, step=1)`. 4. Remove the rigid body world with `bpy.ops.rigidbody.world_remove()` so the motion is purely keyframe-driven. 5. Save the result to `answer.blend`. Requirements: =============== 1. All 10 mesh objects `Domino01..Domino10` exist. 2. `scene.rigidbody_world` is either `None` or disabled (i.e., the simulation has been pre-baked to keyframes and the world removed). 3. Each of the 10 dominoes has `animation_data.action` with at least one keyframe on `location` and at least one keyframe on rotation (`rotation_euler` or `rotation_quaternion`). 4. At `scene.frame_set(1)`, each domino's world-space Z (`matrix_world.translation.z`) is approximately `1.0` (within 0.1). 5. At `scene.frame_set(120)`, each domino's world-space Z is less than `0.5` (i.e., has fallen from its initial height of 1.0 by at least 0.5 BU).
